correctness.rationale: Reconstruction from the primary SWATS equations gives the displayed first and second Adam-phase steps exactly. Substituting the proposed \(x_0\) and \(\varepsilon\) yields \(p_1=-qx_0\), \(p_2=-qx_1\), hence \(\gamma_1=\gamma_2=q\) and \(\lambda_2/(1-b^2)=q\). The source criterion is checked for \(k>1\), so it fires at step 2. With \(\beta_1=0\), the switched phase is ordinary scalar gradient descent with multiplier \(1-q\), whose modulus exceeds one. A fresh independent numerical replay over multiple interior \(b\) values reproduced the exact identities to floating-point tolerance; the infinite family is established algebraically, not by the replay.
correctness.risk: The theorem is deliberately restricted to the no-first-moment mode; it does not claim the default \(\beta_1=0.9\) has the same construction.

source_inspections.title: Improving Generalization Performance by Switching from Adam to SGD

value.rationale: SWATS is designed to learn both when to switch and what SGD rate to use. Showing that perfect stationarity can certify an arbitrarily unstable scalar rate isolates a structural mismatch between temporal agreement and dynamical safety and directly motivates a curvature- or magnitude-sensitive safeguard.
value.risk: The result is a sharp diagnostic counterexample, not a prevalence claim for neural-network training.

final_claim: For source SWATS on the deterministic scalar quadratic \(f(x)=x^2/2\) in the source-supported \(\beta_1=0\) mode, every prescribed \(q>2\) admits positive \(\varepsilon\), interior \(\beta_2\), and an initialization for which the first two projection estimates equal \(q\) exactly, the bias-corrected monitor triggers at its first eligible step, and the selected SGD rate \(q\) is unstable, so the switched iterates diverge geometrically.
limitations: No claim for default \(\beta_1=0.9\), stochastic gradients, or typical training trajectories.
The parameter-dependent initialization is used as an exact adversarial construction.
